newsitem.title: USA: US bank stocks clobbered by interest rate fears.
newsitem.headline: US bank stocks clobbered by interest rate fears.

text.p: Bank stocks took even more of a beating than the broader markets Thursday, in response to higher interest rates in the bond markets, analysts said.
While the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 101.21 points to 6938.16, Citicorp tumbled 3-7/8 to 118-3/4.
NationsBank Corp was off 2-5/8 at 60-1/8 and Chase Manhattan Corp was down 2-3/4 to 101.
"Banks are down; all stocks are down; the world is down," said Raphael Soifer, an analyst at Brown Brothers Harriman.
"But banks are having a very bad day because bonds are down and there's some interest rate fears," he said.
The 30-year bond was off 1-5/32 to yield 6.98 percent in afternoon trade.

Bob Becker, an analyst with Argus Research said "The pullback in bank and financial stocks reflects the increase in bond yields that we have seen throughout the day. The market is taking the position that 'Gee, the economy is very strong -- and the door for interest rate increases is still open.' That's a typical reaction," he continued.
But Becker questions whether that reaction is justified.
"The banking industry is still strong," he maintained.
Soifer said the drop in bank stocks is also related to profit taking from earlier in the week.
